properties.inspection_comments: Purpose: To conduct a food safety inspection in accordance with WAC Chapter 246-215. Due to 35 or more red points, a follow-up inspection will be conducted for the red item violations noted in this inspection report. A fee of $240 will be assessed by mail for all follow-up inspections. If repeated red item violations are observed at a follow-up inspection, an additional follow-up inspection will be required. Notes: - Be sure that single-use gloves are being discarded after use and are not washed, reused, or saved for any reason. - Ensure that food safety rating sign remains visible for all guests upon entry into facility. - Discussed with PIC using only metal pans and lids for better cold holding inside prep top coolers and salsa on ice. *Continuation of #16 violation: Overview of the process if there are repeat red violations cited during future inspections: 4th inspection with repeated red item violation • Charged educational visit with all staff ($240/hour). • Letter to owner with next steps. 5th inspection with repeated red item violation • Facility closed for 24 hours. • Charged pre-opening inspection ($360). • Informal administrative conference at Tacoma -Pierce County Health Department. • Create risk control plan with inspector. • Charged follow-up inspection ($240). 6th inspection with repeated red item violation • Facility closed for 24 hours. • Charged pre-opening inspection ($360). • Formal administrative conference ($840). • Probation for 6 months. -Five additional inspections ($480 each). -Facility is closed if a probation violation is cited. Compliance Schedule OBSERVATIONS AND CORRECTIVE ACTIONS You must complete the following items by the due date listed below . Your inspector will do a compliance inspection . If these items are not corrected, you will be billed for the inspection. Violations cited must be corrected within the time frames specified . Complete ByItem Number 09/24/2026 2600 Compliance with valid permit; operating and risk control plans and required written procedures. 2600 Observed unapproved homestyle Cosori dehydrator and house dried orange slices in bar area. Per PIC, facility got dehydrator and started dehydrating fruit approximately a month prior. No changes may be made to the approved floor plan, menu, equipment , or processes without prior written approval from the health department. You must have plan review approval before you change your menu or procedures . You can find a plan review application at www.tpchd.org/healthy-places/food-safety/opening-a-food-business. Call (253) 649-1706 if you need assistance. Remove the dehydrator and in-house dehydrated fruit from facility .Facility may purchase dehydrated fruit from an approved, commercial wholesale source. Discussed that if facility would like to go through plan review to add a dehydrator to approved processes, unit would need to be of commercial or NSF grade. *A compliance order has been issued to remove the unapproved dehydrator and in -house dehydrated food from facility immediately. Failure to remove the unapproved items immediately will result in a $240 non-compliance fee. Contact your inspector with questions or if you need more time to complete these items. Tacoma - Pierce County Health Department 3629 South D Street, MS 1059 Tacoma , WA 98418 Fax: (253) 649-1728Inspector : Dylan Caverly
